```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(AKCatchments)
```

Every value the package adds comes from someone else's data set. This
vignette covers what you owe the providers when you publish or share
results (references, acknowledgements, terms of use), the one download
that needs an account (the RGI glaciers, with a free Earthdata Login), and
the others that need anything at all. The tables below are made
from the package's own catalogue when the vignette is built, so they match
what `ak_layers()` and `ak_citations()` return.

## 1. Citing the layers you used

`ak_citations()` reads a catchment object's provenance record (which
layers were added, and when) and returns the references for each, the
provider's terms in short, and any acknowledgement text the provider asks
for; with `bibtex` it also writes a BibTeX file for a reference manager.

```{r cite-x, eval = FALSE}
refs <- ak_citations(x, bibtex = "catchments.bib")
unique(refs$reference)                                       # the reference list
unique(refs$acknowledgement[nzchar(refs$acknowledgement)])   # text for the acknowledgements
```

Long tables (daily weather, snow-off, projections, NDVI) carry their own
provenance: pass the table as `x`, or name the layers. Without `x`, name
the layers as `"layer"` (the default variant) or `"layer/variant"`:

```{r cite-layers}
refs <- ak_citations(layers = c("permafrost", "glaciers"))
refs[, c("layer", "key", "doi")]
cat(unique(refs$reference), sep = "\n\n")
```

AKCatchments itself is always the first row. A few things to check by
hand:

- **Access dates.** References to live services (StreamStats, Soil Data
  Access, the fire perimeters, SNAP, AKTEMP, PRISM, the USGS water data
  APIs) carry the date the layer was added to `x`, or today's date for
  layers named in `layers`. Several providers (PRISM, NRCS, USGS
  StreamStats) ask for it.
- **Which flowline source.** The `flowlines` layer lists every source the
  package can use (3DHP, NHD, TDX-Hydro, GEOGLOWS, MERIT-Basins,
  HydroRIVERS); keep the one you used (`snap_reference` in
  `ak_delineate()`, or `source` in `ak_flowlines()`).
- **AKTEMP providers.** Stream temperatures are credited to each data
  provider: replace `[providers]` with the organisations whose series you
  used (in the `ak_obs_temperature()` output).
- **The catchments' DEM.** Terrain attributes are cited through the
  catchment layer (the DEM they were delineated on) plus WhiteboxTools.

## 2. Downloads

Every layer downloads on first use into the cache (`ak_cache_dir()`) and is
read from there afterwards; `ak_prefetch(x, layers)` fetches them up front.
Only the RGI glaciers need an account.

| layer | needs | notes |
|---|---|---|
| Glaciers (RGI 7.0, NSIDC) | a free Earthdata Login, in a `.netrc` file | section 2.1; or download by hand (2.2) |
| Permafrost, ground ice (Jorgenson et al. 2008) | nothing | 13 MB zip from the North Slope Science Catalog |
| Permafrost probability (Pastick et al. 2015) | the archive package or 7-Zip | 777 MB 7-Zip archive from ScienceBase |
| USGS daily values | nothing; an API key (`API_USGS_PAT`) raises the hourly limit | `vignette("observations")` |
| Everything else | nothing | |

### 2.1 Glaciers with your Earthdata Login

NSIDC distributes the Randolph Glacier Inventory behind NASA's Earthdata
Login, from its HTTPS file system (`daacdata.apps.nsidc.org`). The package
downloads the Alaska file (`RGI2000-v7.0-G-01_alaska.zip`) the way NSIDC's
[programmatic access guide](https://nsidc.org/data/user-resources/help-center/programmatic-access-guide-data-daacdataapps)
does it with curl: your Earthdata Login username and password from a
`.netrc` file, and a session cookie. That guide documents the username and
password for this server, not Earthdata Login tokens, so the package
doesn't use a token. Once the file is in the cache, the login isn't needed
again.

1. **Make an account.** Register (free) at
   <https://urs.earthdata.nasa.gov>.
2. **Put the login in a netrc file**, as step 1 of NSIDC's guide says: a
   file named `.netrc` in your home folder (on Windows, `_netrc` in
   `C:\Users\<you>`), with this line:

    ```
    machine urs.earthdata.nasa.gov login <username> password <password>
    ```

    Open the file in an editor (typing the password into the R console
    would keep it in your history):

    ```{r netrc, eval = FALSE}
    netrc <- if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") file.path(Sys.getenv("USERPROFILE"), "_netrc") else "~/.netrc"
    file.edit(netrc)               # add the line above and save
    Sys.chmod(netrc, "600")        # Mac and Linux: readable by you only
    ```

    The password is stored as plain text, as NSIDC's method requires, so
    keep the file in your home folder, out of project folders and anything
    you share or sync to a repository. If you already have a netrc file with
    an `urs.earthdata.nasa.gov` line (from other NASA download tools),
    there is nothing to do.
3. **Download.** The first glacier call downloads and unzips the file into
   the cache's `rgi/` folder:

    ```{r rgi, eval = FALSE}
    ak_prefetch(x, layers = "glaciers")   # status "ok" and the shapefile's path
    x <- ak_glaciers(x)
    ```

Without the netrc line, `ak_glaciers()` stops and `ak_prefetch()` reports
`manual`, with these instructions. If NSIDC answers with the Earthdata login
page, the username or password in the file is wrong. For other problems,
NSIDC User Services (nsidc@nsidc.org) answers questions on programmatic
access.

### 2.2 Glaciers by hand

Without a netrc file: download `RGI2000-v7.0-G-01_alaska.zip` from
<https://nsidc.org/data/nsidc-0770> (*Data Access & Tools*, signed in to
Earthdata Login), and unzip it into the folder given by
`ak_cache_dir("rgi")`, or keep it elsewhere and pass `path` to
`ak_glaciers()`. RGI 6.0 region 01 works the same way.

### 2.3 Jorgenson et al. (2008) permafrost map

The shapefile is downloaded from the North Slope Science Catalog
(dataset 1725) into `ak_cache_dir("jorgenson_2008")`. If the catalog's link
changes, the download fails with a message: download the zip from
<https://catalog.northslopescience.org/dataset/1725>, unzip it into that
folder, or pass `path` to `ak_permafrost()`.

## 3. Terms of use

Most of the data are US federal works in the public domain, with credit
requested. The others set conditions:

- **Attribution text.** PRISM and the Copernicus DEM require a set
  notice, GEOGLOWS and SNAP/CMIP6 ask for one, and USGS, DGGS and the BLM
  ask for credit; the text is in the `acknowledgement` column of
  `ak_citations()`.
- **Citing in a set form, and telling the provider.** NSIDC (glaciers)
  asks for the data set citation in the text and the reference list, and
  that publications using the data be reported to NSIDC User Services
  ([data use policy](https://nsidc.org/about/data-use-and-copyright)).
  Daymet asks for every product and tool used to be cited: the data set,
  the Single Pixel Extraction Tool and the method paper.
- **Creative Commons licences.** The ACCS alder maps, the RGI and GEOGLOWS
  are CC BY 4.0 (share and adapt with attribution); TDX-Hydro is CC BY-SA
  4.0 (data derived from it, if shared, must carry the same licence);
  MERIT-Basins is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (no commercial use).
- **No licence stated.** The Jorgenson et al. (2008) map and the NPS
  Wrangell-St. Elias land cover state no licence: cite them, and ask the
  authors (or NPS) before redistributing the maps themselves.
- **Redistributing derived tables.** Confirm with PRISM and SNAP before
  publishing tables derived from their grids as a data set of their own
  (the `redistributable` column of `ak_layers()`).

These are summaries; the provider's page (the `terms_url` column) is the
authority.

```{r terms, echo = FALSE}
d <- ak_layers(details = TRUE)
d$terms_url <- gsub("(https?://[^; ]+)", "<\\1>", d$terms_url)
knitr::kable(d[, c("layer", "variant", "licence", "terms", "terms_url", "redistributable")],
             col.names = c("layer", "variant", "licence", "terms", "terms page", "redistributable"))
```

## 4. Every layer's references

```{r all-refs, echo = FALSE}
refs <- ak_citations()
refs <- refs[!duplicated(paste(refs$layer, refs$variant, refs$key)), ]
knitr::kable(data.frame(layer = paste0(refs$layer, ifelse(nzchar(refs$variant), paste0(" (", refs$variant, ")"), "")),
                        reference = refs$reference))
```
